question: Does the Q4_K LM-head shared-memory activation cache (0e0c5276) improve complete-request latency on AMD Strix Halo Chrome/Vulkan without changing tokens, text or lifecycle?

arms.A: HEAD 0428c15a with src/gpu/kernels/lm_head_argmax_q4k.wgsl and its kernel-ref digest reverted to 0e0c5276^ (no other change)

design.unit: one independent Node process launching one fresh headless Chrome process, opening the model once
design.order: blocks alternate ABBA and BAAB; 10 blocks = 20 processes per arm
design.browser: Google Chrome stable via Playwright channel=chrome, --use-angle=vulkan --enable-features=Vulkan
design.contention: gpu_busy_percent sampled every 100 ms by the parent during each process; Reploid native participants left running and recorded

primaryMetric: per-process median of the 5 warm complete-request wall times (generate() call start to iterator end)
secondaryMetrics: decode and prefill stats from getStats()
analysis: paired by block position: log(B/A) for adjacent A,B processes within each block (2 pairs per block, 20 pairs). Report mean, median, 95% t-interval and 10000-resample percentile bootstrap interval of the mean log ratio, expressed as percent change.

promotionRule.parity: every request in every process of both arms yields identical token IDs and text; A and B must match each other
promotionRule.lifecycle: every process completes unload() and destroyDevice() without error, and Chrome exits cleanly
promotionRule.latency: upper bound of the 95% bootstrap interval of mean warm complete-request percent change (B vs A) is below 0
promotionRule.otherwise: retain the kernel measurement separately; do not claim a complete-request improvement on AMD

crossPlatform: The M3 Metal half runs on mac-host with this same contract; AMD alone cannot promote the change for Metal.
